What is NID DAT Entrance Exam?

NID DAT stands for NID Design Aptitude Test. It is conducted by the National Institute of Design at the national level for admission to B.Des and M.Des programmes at NID institutes in India . NID DAT evaluates candidates on the basis of creativity, problem-solving skills, innovative skills, visual perception, etc.

It is not mandatory to take coaching to get a good rank in NID DAT. It is because the entrance exam will test the creative, drawing, and innovative skills of the candidate. Now, a coaching institute cannot exactly teach you to be creative or become innovative. Instead, with a little effort these skills can learn these skills yourself. Also, a major thrust of the design aptitude test is to evaluate the drawing skills of the candidate. So, make it a point to work on your design skills, including learning how to draw lines, shadow, figure, gesture, cartoon drawing, etc. When practicing drawing, also keep a tab on the drawing speed, as it will help you complete the paper in the allotted time.

The application fee of NID DAT 2026 for the B. Des for General, General-EWS, OBC-NCL candidates is INR 3,000. SC, ST, PwD candidates only ned to pay INR 1,500. However note that the application fees for overseas candidates seeking admission to supernumerary seats is INR 5000. In case of the M.Des programme, the application fees for General, General-EWS, OBC-NCL candidates applying for one discipline is INR 3,000. If two disciplines are chosen, the application fee is INR 6000. Meanwhile, SC, ST, PwD candidate need to pay INR 1,500 for one discipline, and INR 3000 for two disciplines.
The NID DAT 2026 application form is now open.

The NID Entrance Exam is considered to be one of the toughest design entrance exam conducted in the country. In NID DAT, more weightage is given to subjective, drawing related questions. Thus, candidates need to be extremely creative and have a clear understanding of their concepts when appearing for the NID exam.
For preparing the final results for the  B. Des program, the DAT Prelims will be allocated 40% weightage, while DAT Mains will be given 60%.
During the DAT Mains, which comprises a Studio Test, the candidate is tested hands-on and have to show their drawing abilities, creativity, innovativeness, and material-handling ability.

The admission to the NIDs is conducted through a Design Aptitude Test (DAT). The DAT is a two-stage exam.

The candidate has to first appear in DAT Prelims and then, if shortlisted, have to appear in DAT Mains. The final merit list for admission will be prepared by giving weightage to both DAT Prelims and DAT Mains. If a candidate appear in DAT Prelims, but doesn’t appear in DAT Mains, he or she will not be considered for admission.

The NID DAT 2026 Mains exam for B. Des will comprise a Studio Test. The Studio Test will be conducted in offline mode. The candidate will be given the option to select test centre before the test. Test centres will be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis. DAT Mains exam for the B. Des programme will be conducted in April 2026. Meanwhile, DAT Mains for the M.Des programme will comprise a Studio Test and an Online Interview. The Studio Test will be conducted on offline mode, while the Personal Interview will be conducted online.

value: How to prepare for Design Aptitude Test (DAT)?

blocks.value: A candidate would ideally need around 6 months or so to prepare for the NID DAT exam. He can take up to 3 months if his fundamentals are strong.

Along with following the official NID DAT exam pattern and syllabus, do these tasks to prepare for the NID Entrance exam:

value: Solve sample papers - You can start solving sample papers very early on in your preparation, for instance, after completing a chapter.
Solve previous years’ papers - This exercise will help you get an idea about the nature and structure of the exam, including difficulty level, types of questions asked, marking scheme, and much more.
Take mock tests - Mocks are usually taken closer to the exam date. It will help you fine-tune your preparation and fix the mental aspect of taking an entrance exam.
Take notes during study - This exercise will not only help you stay focused, but also help you jot down important and difficult points. This, in turn will make revision easier and quicker.

blocks.value: What is the Procedure for NID Counselling 2026?
The following steps explain the Counselling Procedure in detail.
Step 1: Check your Qualifying Status
You must clear the NID DAT exam to attend the NID DAT Counselling. The qualifying status can be checked after logging into the NID DAT result portal.
Step 2: Submission of Campus Preference (only for B.Des applicants)

B.Des candidates need to submit their choice of campuses. The entries must be in the order of priority . Note that if no options are selected, the candidate may be disqualified. The candidate will be asked to make a campus selection based on:
Note: M.Des candidates are not required to submit campus preferences.
Step 3: Seat Allocation

NID Seat Allotment will be done keeping the factors like seat intake, merit rank of applicants, campus preferences opted for, and category. Once a seat has been allocated, the candidate has to confirm their seat by:
a) Payment of non-refundable seat-confirmation fees

value: INR 30,000 (online payment) + convenience fees (as applicable) for General, Gen EWS, OBC-NCL, SC, ST, and PwD candidates
INR 75,000 (online payment) + convenience fees (as applicable) for Overseas candidates

blocks.value: b) Uploading of documents
The following documents are required to be uploaded as a single PDF file with a maximum file size of 10 MB:

value: A valid photo ID (Aadhaar Card, Election ID, PAN Card, Driving License, or Passport)
Birth Certificate OR School Leaving Certificate
Gen-EWS/ OBC-NCL/ ST/ ST Certificate (if applicable)
Passport (if applied under the Supernumerary category)

blocks.value: Important Notes:

value: If the Class 12 marks sheet has not been issued, a digital copy of the same, duly attested by the school principal, must be uploaded. Candidates whose results are pending must provide a genuine certificate issued by the school principal, explicitly stating the Roll No. and the projected date of the announcement of results.
For those candidates who finished their Class 12 (or equivalent) final examinations outside of India or from a Board not listed in the Admission Handbook, they must submit an equivalent certificate.

Candidates who do not pay the non-refundable token fees within the period specified above will have their provisional seat allocations canceled. In order of merit, that seat will be given to the next qualified candidate.

Candidates who fail to provide the required documents within the designated period, even after paying, will have their provisional seat allocation canceled. The seat will subsequently be assigned in order of merit to the next qualifying candidate.
Even after the seat confirmation, the candidate will stand a chance to participate in other rounds of counseling for which he/she will have to submit their willingness to do so.

blocks.value: Step 4: Document Verification

All the documents uploaded by the candidates will be cross-checked against the information provided at the time of online registration. If any discrepancy is found, the candidate will be disqualified.
Step 5: Issue of Provisional Offer Letter for Admission

Upon verification of documents, the candidate will be issued Provisional Offer Letters of Admission. The candidate has to next pay the NIDs directly; payment-related information will be communicated to the candidate. The provisional offer letter for B.Des will be issued in the second week of June 2026, while the provisional offer letter for M.Des will be released in the third week of May 2026.

value: Payment of fees and uploading of documents: Candidates who are allotted seats have to pay the tuition fee for Semester I and upload the required documents before the last date.

What happens if the candidate gets shortlisted for two disciplines (M.Des): If the candidate has applied in two disciplines and gets shortlisted in both disciplines, in that case, the candidate is allotted a seat in the discipline marked as first preference .

Applied for two disciplines but shortlisted for discipline marked as preference 02: In case the candidate has applied for TWO disciplines but is shortlisted only for the discipline marked as preference 02, the candidate will be allotted a seat in the discipline marked as preference 02.

Applied for two disciplines, and eligible for both disciplines: In case the candidate has applied for TWO disciplines and is eligible for both but gets shortlisted for only the discipline marked as preference 02, then the candidate will be allocated a seat in the discipline marked as preference 02.

blocks.value: However, if there is a vacancy in the discipline marked as Preference 01, then by default, the candidate will be upgraded to the discipline marked as Preference 01. Also, the previous allotment is canceled (Preference 02), and the vacant seat is allocated to the candidate next in the order of merit.

Note that candidates belonging to reserved categories will also be considered for admission under the general category. However, candidates from general categories can't apply for admission under reserved categories. The candidate has to select their admission category at the time of filling out the NID that application form. Also, the candidate has to produce supporting documents at the time of admission. If the candidate fails to produce their category Certificate then he or she will be considered for admission under the general category.

faqs.question: How many seats are available for Interior Designing in NID?
faqs.answer: The Interior Design programme is offered both for the BDes and MDes courses. At the BDes level, the Interior Design programme is offered under the faculty of Industrial Design, with a specialisation in Furniture and Interior Design. There are currently 13 seats for the programme. At the master's level, MDes in Furniture & Interior Design course is offered at the NID Ahmedabad campus. The intake capacity for the MDes programme is currently 19 seats. Admission to the Interior Design programme (both Bachelor's and master's) at the NIDs will be through the NID DAT exam.

faqs.question: When will the NID DAT 2026 Prelims exam be conducted?
faqs.answer: The National Institute of Design (NID) conducted the DAT Prelims exam on December 21, 2025. The B.Des exam was held around 10 am - 1 pm; meanwhile, the M.Des exam was 10 am - 12.30 am. Prep Tips for NID DAT (Prelims) 2026

NID DAT and NIFT are likely two of the most popular and difficult design entrance exams in the country. So, one needs to be very particular about one's exam preparation strategy, so that hiccups and errors don't derail the set goal.
Read below the tips to prepare for the NID DAT exam.
1. Get familiar with the NID Exam 2026 Syllabus

There is no negative marking in NID DAT Prelims. However, if MSQ questions are asked in the exam, then the weightage allotted to them may vary from 0.5 marks to 4 marks for each question.

blocks.value: 4. Prepare a timetable

Like any exam, to prepare well for the NID 2026 entrance exam, aspirants need to prepare a timetable. Not only this, candidates are advised to prepare a daily, weekly, as well as a monthly prep plan for NID DAT Prelims. Further, candidates should attempt to complete their syllabus as soon as possible and keep the last month before the exam for revision and solving as many past years’ question papers, sample papers, and mock tests as they can.
5. Solve NID Sample and Previous years' Question papers

Candidates should attempt to solve as many NID entrance exam question papers as they can get their hands on. Solving actual question papers for the NID entrance exam would help candidates know the format of questions asked in the exam, along with understanding the exam pattern. Past years’ question papers for the NID entrance exam also help candidates in identifying important topics, resulting in aspirants securing higher marks in this design entrance test.
6. Solve NID Sample Papers and Mock tests

Candidates can test their knowledge of topics asked in the NID entrance exam by solving as many sample papers and mock tests as possible. Attempting mock tests as well as sample papers also helps candidates in making a strategy for time management when solving the question paper for the exam.
7. Practice drawing for the NID DAT Entrance Test
Practice drawing whatever catches your imagination, or anything around you, be it your mom’s kitchen, the street you visit to buy daily groceries, the mall, or the security guard performing his duty.

value: There are various forms of drawing, like caricature, photorealism, figure, cartoon, animation, doodling, gestural, and technical, etc. Practice each form of drawing. Live sketching and still drawings also open up one's hands.

During the exam, it is always a good idea to make a light outline, rather than putting rigid lines or curves. This way, there will be little need to erase and redraw. This, in turn, will keep the copy clean and tidy.

Another tip is to learn the art of using dry color, as they are easier to handle and take less time. Do some research about color rendering, theory, emotions, etc. Be original in your creations, because it is what will impress the jury. Conversely, copying designs from others can sink your boat pretty fast.

blocks.value: Prep Tips for NID DAT (Mains) 2026

NID Mains exam will include Studio Test and In-Person Sensitivity Test for B.Des candidates. Test pattern for NID DAT Mains is such that candidates are asked to make a sketch or model in THREE hours . After the studio test, the candidate will also have to appear in a personal interview.
Tips to prepare for NID DAT 2026 (Mains) are given below.

value: Develop Observation & Visualization Skills - Remember that DAT Mains will not evaluate how much information you carry in your brain, but rather how effectively and creatively you can use that information to create something beautiful and awe-inspiring.
One way to develop your creative side is to be conscious of your existence and observe objects with a keen eye.

Solve Sample Papers - This is one of the best tools to prepare for the design entrance exam. To begin with, sample papers will help you improve your problem-solving ability and help you get a better understanding of the concepts. The candidate can start solving sample papers from the very early stages of their exam preparation. Further, using a timer, the candidate may also be able to work on their time management skills through the sample papers.

Work on your speed - While sample papers are a great tool to work on one’s speed, the candidate may also take mock tests to hone this skill. Mocks are usually taken closer to the entrance exam. When solving a problem, the candidate must try to solve it as quickly as possible. An in depth understanding of the concepts and their relation to other concepts will aid in faster problem-solving. So, you must also make it a point to ensure that you properly master all the key concepts of the various topics.

Work on your general awareness - You need to know what is happening nationally and internationally, especially regarding events of importance. So, make it a habit to read leading daily newspapers, for instance, the Hindu, Indian Express, TOI, etc. Focus on the editorial and opinion pieces.

faqs.question: Can I request to change my allotted NID DAT exam centre?
faqs.answer: NID Centre can be changed only at the time of NID Application edit Window. After this, no centre can be changed.

faqs.question: How many NID 2026 Mains exam centres are there?
faqs.answer: NID Mains Exam will consist of Studio Test and Interview. NID 2026 Mains exam will be conducted at Ahmedabad, Bengaluru and Gandhinagar.

faqs.question: How can I find details of NID DAT 2026 Exam center allocated to me?
faqs.answer: Details of NID DAT 2026 Exam centre, name, address, and reporting time are given in the NID DAT 2026 Admit card. DAT Prelims admit card was available for download from December 11, 2025.

faqs.question: Will there be a baggage counter at NID DAT 2026 center?
faqs.answer: No, National Institute of Design may not make any arrangements for a baggage counter. So, candidates must bear this in mind when packing for NID DAT Prelims exam. It is recommended that candidate only pack bare essentials and not bring unnecessary stuff to exam centre. Also, expensive items like smartphones, jewellery, gadgets, etc., should be better left at home.

faqs.question: In how many cities will the NID DAT 2026 (Prelims) exam be conducted?
faqs.answer: The NID DAT 2026 (Prelims) exam will be conducted in the first week of January 2026. The exam will be conducted in the following 22 cities - Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Bhopal, Bhubaneshwar, Chandigarh, Chennai, Dehradun, Guwahati, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Kochi, Kolkata, Kurukshetra, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, New Delhi, Patna, Raipur, Ranchi, Thiruvananthapuram, Vijayawada. The candidate has to select their choice of exam city at the time of filling out the NID DAT 2026 Application form. Note that an exam city may have one or more test centres. The allotment of exam centres will be made considered available seats in respective centres and choice of the candidate.

faqs.question: What is the reporting time at NID DAT Exam centre?
faqs.answer: The reporting time for NID DAT will be mentioned in the Admit card, along with gate closing time, and exam timings and date. The candidate needs to report for the DAT Prelims exam at 8 am. The gates of the exam center will close at 9:30 AM (or 30 minutes before the commencement of the exam). After that no candidate will be allowed inside the exam hall. NID DAT Exam timings: B.Des - 10 am - 1 pm M.Des - 10 am - 12.30 pm

faqs.answer: The NID DAT exam is conducted in two stages. First, the candidate has to appear in DAT Prelims, and if shortlisted has to appear in DAT Mains. The results of DAT Prelims for B.Des will be declared on April 07, 2026, while results for the M.Des programme will be declared on February 12, 2026. The candidate will be able to check their results by logging into the result portal using their email ID and date of birth. Such candidates who get shortlisted have to next appear in DAT Mains.
